newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka considering elections in northern Jaffna.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka considering elections in northern Jaffna.

text.p: Sri Lanka's government, fresh from its landslide victory in last week's local council poll, may hold elections for local bodies in the former Tamil rebel stronghold of Jaffna, government sources said on Wednesday.
"There is a strong possibility that elections (for local bodies) will be held in Jaffna," a senior government official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters.
The ruling People's Alliance coalition swept the March 21 election, winning 194 of the 238 councils at stake, taking 49 percent of the total votes polled.
The main opposition United National Party could muster only 43 councils, but secured 41.3 percent of the total vote.
Elections were not held in the north and east where government troops are battling the separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels.
Minority Tamil political parties told government authorities that the two regions, large areas of which are under rebel control, were not conducive for a free and fair poll.

The LTTE are waging a 13-year-old war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's majority Sinhalese north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war. The LTTE says the number is higher.
"It is only fair we give the choice of the vote to people of the north and the east, just as we did to people of the rest of the country," the government official said.
"(An election) would be a good way to bring the people of these areas into mainstream politics, regardless of the situation there," he added.

It was not immediately clear if the election would be held in both the north and the east, but the northern Jaffna district, completely recaptured by the armed forces from the rebels, was a distinct possibility, he added.
The present term of office for local bodies in Jaffna ends in July and elections will have to be held before this date, he said. None of the local bodies in the district are currently functioning.
But a Tamil group said it would lobby the government for more time if it decides to go ahead with local polls there.
"The situation immediately is not conducive for a free and fair poll," said Douglas Devananda, leader of the Eelam People's Democratic Party, which has strong presence in Jaffna.

"More than street lights and garbage collection, the people of Jaffna need peace and an honourable settlement to this war. Neither we, nor the government, can offer them that right now," Devananda, a former rebel turned politician, told Reuters.
The LTTE were not immediately available for comment, but its official radio has belittled the government victory.
"The government's attractive campaign has deceieved the voters," the clandestine Voice of Tigers radio, monitored in the northern frontline town of Vavuniya, said on Monday.
It said the government has now been pushed into a situation where it could not decide whether to continue its war against the LTTE or push ahead with its peace proposals.
Last week's victory was widely seen as a public endorsement of the government's peace proposals, which will grant wide autonomy to minorities and are aimed at ending the ethnic war.
"The government has made no concrete moves yet with the peace plan and we have nothing to go to the people (of the north) with," Devananda said.
The peace plan is currently being considered by a parliamentary select committee and is expected to be presented to the house for a vote in November.
